summary: This consolidated entry captures the maturation of system stability, moving from performance-focused instrumentation to holistic autonomous maintenance. It bridges the evolution of the Adaptive Throughput Controller (ATC) and SCCL governance with foundational memory management techniques, establishing a unified framework where telemetry-driven control theory and semantic validation ensure monotonic architectural health.
key_learnings: PID controllers and SCCL patterns form a robust foundation for autonomous system stability.
System health is maximized by prioritizing the removal of stale assets and proactive semantic gating over raw throughput.
Telemetry and control theory are essential for mitigating instability in autonomous agents.
Memory compression and incremental indexing are interdependent pillars for maintaining long-term architectural integrity.
